questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people skip breakfast
How to make new words in English
Feeling angry when you're hungry, and why
Why social media makes so many people angry these days
questions.why: Neil says the topic 'is all about feeling angry when you are hungry'.

questions.q: Why is Neil feeling grumpy at the start?
options: He hasn't eaten yet
Dan was late
He forgot the script
He slept badly
questions.why: Neil says he hasn't had the chance to eat yet 'and it's making me a bit grumpy'.

He was doing research for the programme
The canteen was closed
He forgot his lunch
questions.why: Neil says 'I was doing some research for today's topic'.

questions.q: What does Sophie Medlin say about 'hanger'?
options: It was invented by scientists at King's College London
It is not a real thing
It only affects children
Science has long known hunger causes irritability
questions.why: She says 'We've long recognised that hunger leads to irritability - in science.'

questions.q: What does Dan add about the word 'hangry'?
options: It first appeared in the 1990s, before social media
It was first used on Twitter by a famous hungry celebrity
It comes from another language
It is not in any dictionary
questions.why: Dan says the word actually appeared in the 1990s, a little before social media.

questions.q: According to Sophie Medlin, what happens in our body when blood sugar drops?
options: We produce less adrenalin
It produces more fight or flight hormones
Our brain stops working
We feel more relaxed and sleepy, so we get less angry
questions.why: She says as blood sugars drop, 'we increase our cortisol and adrenalin'.

questions.q: Why do hunger and anger feel similar, according to Medlin?
options: Because we eat when we are angry
Because both make us tired
Because angry people forget to eat
Because the same brain chemicals trigger both
questions.why: She says the chemicals that trigger hunger 'are the same ones that trigger for anger'.

questions.q: What does Dan suggest about Neil near the end?
options: He has calmed down
He should go on a diet
He is still hangry
He is being too polite
questions.why: Dan says 'I can see that you're still a bit hangry Neil.'
